title: Pack install integrity: empty owned-copy shadows the plugin and is blessed with a false integrity hash
description:
From the 2026-08-02 deep review (pass 1, HIGH, empirically reproduced). Root cause of the "empty box" problem.

**The defect.** `src/pack-apply.js:266-275` selects the owned source with `searchPath.map(base => join(base, bareId)).find(dir => existsSync(dir))`. That tests only that a DIRECTORY EXISTS — it never checks the directory is a real owned skill copy (no `SKILL.md` check, unlike `src/assimilate.js`). Before TASK-181 there was a single `sourceRoot` so there was nothing to shadow; the multi-root search path TASK-181 introduced makes this load-bearing.

Reproduced verbatim on this branch — a consumer fixture with `PROJECT.md` plus an EMPTY `assimilated-skills/watch/`, run through `node bin/pack-ctl.js reconcile-apply --repo-root <fixture>` with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` / `HIVEMIND_OWNED_SOURCE_ROOT` unset:

```
ok= true  planned= 2  installed= 1
installed ids: [["skill:ui-ux-pro-max"],[]]
reports:       [[plugin:frontend-design out-of-scope],[]]   <-- NO report entry for watch
live watch dir exists: true, contents: [], SKILL.md present: false
```

and `integrations.lock.json` gains:

```
"skill:watch": { "pin": "83da59fa78c3eee9e20f515fe75c438bb5166efd",
                 "integrity": "sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855", ... }
```

That integrity value is the SHA-256 of the EMPTY input — an empty tree recorded as a verified copy at the upstream pin. `executeInstall` succeeds without throwing, so nothing lands in `packs[].report`; `reconcilePack`'s `probeSkills` re-derivation drops it from `installed`; the CLI still prints `ok: true`. On re-run `hasStageTimeBaseline` is false (legacy `integrity` only), so the empty dir wins again and the skill stays permanently broken.

This is the silent-failure class TASK-181's AC6 was created to eliminate, reintroduced through the shadowing path the same ticket added.

**Folded in from the same review (same files — kept together deliberately to avoid a second pass over this surface):**

1. **Partial failure reads as success.** `bin/pack-ctl.js:452-455` computes `totalFailure = plannedInstallCount > 0 && installedCount === 0`, so `ok` only falsifies when NOTHING installs. With the two packs shipping today, one soft-failing while the other lands yields `installed_count: 1 / planned_install_count: 2` and `ok: true`. Confirmed by mutation: rewriting the guard to `installedCount < plannedInstallCount` leaves all 30 specs in the two pack-ctl spec files green — the partial branch is untested. A hard-abort also still reports `ok: true`.
2. **Exit-code contract.** `run()` returns `ok: !totalFailure`; `main()` does `const payload = { ok: true, ...result }` then returns normally, so the process exits 0 with `ok:false`, no `code`, no `message`, nothing on stderr — contradicting the module header at `bin/pack-ctl.js:90-94`. The new e2e lock asserts `json.ok === false` but never `result.status`. (This was TASK-182 item 1; it moves here because it is the same code path.)
3. **A spec mutates the real repository.** `tests/e2e/pack-ctl-consumer-source.spec.js:151` runs the WRITE command `reconcile-apply` against the live `REPO_ROOT`. `applyPlan` unconditionally calls `writeLock(lockPath, lock)` on the git-tracked `integrations.lock.json` and `executeInstall` does `rmSync`+`cpSync` under the real `.claude/skills/`. It passes today only because the serializer round-trip happens to be byte-identical — content coincidence, not isolation. Every other spec in the file uses `makeTmpDir`.
4. **Precedence is untested.** No spec seeds two ancestors both holding `assimilated-skills/`, so flipping `ancestorsOf` to root-first (`out.unshift`) leaves all 8 specs in `tests/plugin-root.spec.js` green (mutation-confirmed) — the nearest-ancestor rule that stops a stray high-level `assimilated-skills/` from shadowing the plugin is unlocked. Likewise `applyPlan`'s multi-root search has no test proving local-beats-plugin precedence.
5. **Dead parameter.** `executeInstall` still destructures `sourceRoot` while its only caller passes `sourceRoots` — the `: [sourceRoot]` fallback is unreachable.

**Contested, do NOT treat as settled:** pass 1 flagged the unbounded ancestor walk as MEDIUM; pass 2's verifier REFUTED the same claim (it requires write access to an already-trusted tree). Investigate and record a decision; do not silently adopt either verdict.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first reproduces the empty-box defect: a consumer fixture with an EMPTY assimilated-skills/<id>/ shadowing a valid plugin copy currently installs an empty skill dir, records the empty-tree SHA-256 as its integrity at the upstream pin, and still reports ok:true with no report entry. Capture the red-run output verbatim as the tests-first evidence.

Owned-source selection validates that a candidate directory is a REAL owned skill copy (at minimum a readable SKILL.md, consistent with how src/assimilate.js validates) rather than a bare existsSync directory test. An invalid or empty candidate is skipped in favour of the next entry on the search path, and if NO candidate is valid the resource fails loudly with a report entry naming what was tried.

No false integrity is ever recorded: a skill that did not actually materialize must not gain an integrations.lock.json entry, and in particular the SHA-256 of an empty tree must never be written as a verified copy. Covered by a spec asserting the lockfile after a failed materialize.

The failure is self-healing rather than sticky: after the fix, a re-run against the same fixture must not re-bless the empty directory (the permanently-broken re-run path described in the ticket is closed). Covered by a spec that runs reconcile-apply twice.

Partial materialize failure no longer reports success: the ok predicate distinguishes full success, partial failure, and total failure. A spec exercises 0 < installedCount < plannedInstallCount specifically — mutation of the predicate must break at least one test (the current guard is mutation-transparent).

The CLI's exit code and its documented output contract agree. Decide deliberately whether the code conforms to the bin/pack-ctl.js:90-94 header (code/message + non-zero exit) or the header is rewritten to document the new shape; record the decision in the closing comment. A spec asserts result.status, not just json.ok, so the exit-code gap cannot regress.

tests/e2e/pack-ctl-consumer-source.spec.js no longer runs a mutating command against the live REPO_ROOT — it uses a tmp fixture like every other spec in the file, or is restructured to a read-only assertion. Verify with a deliberately dirtied working tree that the suite no longer rewrites tracked files.

Precedence is locked by specs that would fail under mutation: (a) an ancestor walk seeding TWO ancestors holding assimilated-skills/ proves nearest-first wins, and (b) applyPlan's multi-root search proves a local adoption beats a built-in of the same id. Flipping ancestorsOf to root-first must now fail a test.
executeInstall's dead sourceRoot parameter and its unreachable [sourceRoot] fallback are removed, or the parameter is genuinely reachable and tested. No unreachable defensive branch is left behind.

The contested unbounded-ancestor-walk question is investigated and a decision recorded in the closing comment (harden, bound the walk, or accept with rationale) — pass 1 confirmed it MEDIUM, pass 2 refuted it; the ticket must not close with that disagreement unresolved.
npm run test:all is green; no existing pack/reconcile/assimilate/apply spec regresses; dist/pack-ctl.cjs rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed, with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.
